title: Marguerite and the Ghost
premise: Emrys Whitlock, a whistle-blower living under four names, takes anonymous contracts exposing crimes no one will touch. When a voiceprint he recorded years ago unlocks a black-site server in Kazakhstan, he discovers the extraction of a defector — Marguerite, the scientist whose testimony could topple a transnational surveillance cartel — is actually a trap set by the very people who once employed him. Racing across three countries with his old handler turned hunter on his trail, Emrys must decide whether Marguerite is a witness to save or bait designed to flush him out. At dawn, as the extraction flight prepares to leave, he sacrifices his last identity and his own escape to put her on the plane, surviving only because Marguerite chooses to jump back and pull him from the kill zone. The book ends with both of them nameless together, the server's contents released, and the cartel's fall beginning in earnest.
about_author: Dominic Iversen is the pen name of a former intelligence analyst who spent a decade inside the machinery he now writes about, publishing under an assumed identity since 2016. His thrillers are known for procedural precision, moral ambiguity, and protagonists who pay real prices for doing the right thing.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Emrys Whitlock's POV. Living in Tallinn under his fourth identity, Emrys accepts an anonymous contract: verify a leaked voiceprint against a locked server. The beat is quiet dread — routine work that feels slightly wrong, establishing his paranoid competence and the loneliness of a man who cannot be anyone for long.

chapters.title: The Voice That Answers
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The voiceprint matches: it's his own recording from six years ago, and it unlocks a server holding evidence of a surveillance cartel's assassinations — plus a live extraction dossier for a defector named Marguerite Voss. The emotional beat is vertigo; his past has reached across continents to find him.

chapters.title: Marguerite
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Hiding in Almaty after fleeing the cartel's biometrics division, Marguerite suspects her promised extraction is too easy, too well-funded. She tests her handlers and finds small lies. The beat is wary hope curdling into suspicion — she may be cargo, not a passenger.

chapters.title: The Handler Who Hunts
chapters.summary: Dane Kessler's POV. Emrys's former handler, now working for the cartel, is activated when the server logs show the voiceprint unlock. Dane knows all four of Emrys's names. The beat is cold professional intimacy — the hunter who loved his asset, now obliged to bury him.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in Riga
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Following the dossier's breadcrumbs to Riga, Emrys meets the fixer running the extraction and realizes the flight plan was authored by someone who knew his tradecraft intimately. The beat is rising panic; the trap isn't for Marguerite alone — it's shaped like him.

chapters.title: What the Server Knows
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Emrys decrypts the full archive: Marguerite's defection was engineered by the cartel to lure out every whistle-blower they ever lost, Emrys chief among them. Meanwhile Marguerite finds her own file on the same network. The beat is terrible clarity — both now know she's bait, and neither can walk away.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Against every protocol, Emrys contacts Marguerite directly through a compromised channel; she nearly turns him in before recognizing the voice from the server. They agree to meet in twelve hours, each half-convinced the other is the trap. The beat is fragile trust between two people trained to trust no one.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Emrys and Marguerite's POV, alternating scenes. Evading Kessler's sweep teams through Almaty's night markets and rail yards, they trade truths — her experiments, his betrayals — while planning a decoy route to the airfield. The beat is exhausted intimacy; survival strips them down to what's real.

chapters.title: Dawn Flight
chapters.summary: All three POVs converge at the airfield. Emrys runs the decoy himself, letting Kessler take him so Marguerite boards clean — but Kessler, given the choice between killing Emrys and letting the archive go public, hesitates. Gunfire, a burning hangar, and Marguerite jumping from the plane's steps to drag Emrys clear. The beat is climax: sacrifice met by refusal.

chapters.title: No Names Left
chapters.summary: Shared POV, alternating short sections. Weeks later, the archive detonates across headlines; the cartel's directors scatter. Emrys, officially dead, sheds his fourth name entirely, and Marguerite — testifying under protection — chooses anonymity beside him over reinstatement. The beat is hard-won peace: justice outside the law, paid for in full, and a life begun from zero.
